title: Weisfeiler-Lehman subtree count features
spec: Add a hashed Weisfeiler-Lehman subtree count vector as an extra feature block. For each molecule, start from atom invariants (element, degree, formal charge, aromaticity, H count), run 3 WL refinement iterations over the heavy-atom graph, and hash each (iteration, label) pair with zlib.crc32 into 1024 buckets. Count occurrences per bucket and append the vector to the existing Morgan plus descriptor matrix. Leave the Tanimoto kernel on ECFP bits only. Use the same featurisation for train and test so nothing leaks across folds.

title: IRLS L1-loss kernel regression member
spec: Replace the squared-error kernel ridge member with an absolute-error version fitted by iteratively reweighted least squares. Start from the current Tanimoto plus RBF kernel solution. At each of about 15 iterations, set per-sample weights w_i = 1 / max(|residual_i|, 0.05), solve the weighted system (K + lambda W^-1) alpha = y - mu, and recompute residuals. Keep the same lambda and RBF weight grid search, using the held-out MAE as the selection criterion. This targets the MAE metric directly rather than the squared error the member currently minimises.

title: Applicability-domain shrinkage toward the training mean
spec: Compute, for each test molecule, its maximum Tanimoto similarity to any training molecule (ECFP bits). Let s be that similarity. Blend the final stacked prediction p as p' = mu + w(s)*(p - mu), where mu is the training mean and w(s) = clip((s - 0.3)/0.4, 0, 1). Molecules with no close training analogue are therefore pulled toward the mean, which is the L1-optimal guess under uncertainty, and well-covered molecules keep their model prediction. Calibrate the 0.3 and 0.7 cut points once on the out-of-fold stack predictions by choosing the pair with the lowest mean absolute error, using a coarse grid of 5 values each.

title: Bit-dropout augmentation with test-time averaging
spec: For the random forest and LightGBM members only, create two augmented copies of the training matrix Xa in which each fingerprint bit (the first 2*N_BITS columns) is zeroed independently with probability 0.1, and stack them with the original rows, keeping the labels duplicated. Fit both models on the augmented matrix. At prediction time, average the predictions over the clean test matrix and three copies with 10% of fingerprint bits zeroed using a fixed seed. The kernel member is unchanged.

title: L1-optimal convex meta-learner via linear programming
spec: Replace the positive Ridge meta-learner with an explicit mean-absolute-error fit: find non-negative weights w (one per base learner, plus an intercept b restricted to the range of y) that minimise sum |y_i - (oof_i @ w + b)| subject to w >= 0 and sum(w) = 1. Solve it as a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS), using slack variables for the absolute values. Use the OOF predictions as the design matrix and apply the solved weights to the base learners' test predictions. Fall back to the simple average if the solver fails.

title: kNN residual correction after the stack
spec: After the stacked meta prediction is produced for the test set, compute residuals on the out-of-fold stack predictions (oof meta-predictions minus y) for the training set. For each test molecule, find its training neighbours by Tanimoto similarity on the ECFP bits, keep the k=10 most similar with similarity above 0.4, and add to the prediction a similarity-weighted mean of their OOF residuals scaled by a shrinkage factor of 0.5. If no neighbour passes the threshold, add nothing. Use only the training fold, so no test labels are involved.

title: MinMax (generalised Tanimoto) kernel on count ECFP as the kernel member
spec: Keep the existing kernel-ridge base learner, but replace its bit-vector Tanimoto kernel with the MinMax kernel K(a,b)=sum_i min(a_i,b_i)/sum_i max(a_i,b_i) computed on radius-2 count fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy, 2048 bits). Compute it in numpy by blocks, for example with a loop over bit chunks, so memory stays under 6 GB. Keep the RBF term and the lambda/RBF-weight grid search exactly as they are, and use the MinMax kernel in place of the Tanimoto term in both the grid search and the final fit.

title: Laplacian kernel on the standardised descriptor block
spec: In base_predict, replace the RBF kernel on the z-scored descriptor block with a Laplacian kernel, exp(-gamma * L1 distance), where gamma is 1/(number of descriptors times the mean absolute pairwise distance on the training fold). Keep the summed Tanimoto kernel and the lambda/weight grid unchanged. The L1 distance is less sensitive to outlying descriptor values than the squared Euclidean distance used by the RBF, and the MAE loss may benefit. Compute the pairwise L1 distances with scipy.spatial.distance.cdist to keep the code short.

title: pH 7.4 neutral-fraction feature from ionisable SMARTS
spec: Add one scalar per molecule: the log10 fraction of neutral species at pH 7.4. Use a small hand-written table of pKa values for acids (carboxylic acid ~4.5, tetrazole ~4.9, acyl sulfonamide ~4.5, phenol ~10) and bases (aliphatic amine ~9.5, amidine ~11, pyridine ~5.2). For each matched group, the ionised fraction is 1/(1+10^(pKa-7.4)) for acids and 1/(1+10^(7.4-pKa)) for bases. Sum the log10 neutral fractions over the matched groups, cap the result at -4, and append it to the descriptor block of the LightGBM and random forest inputs. Do not change the kernel members. Keep the code to one SMARTS dictionary and one loop.

title: Pairwise difference learning with anchor averaging
spec: Add a new base learner that models differences between molecules. For each training fold, sample about 20000 random pairs (i, j). Build the difference feature vector as the ECFP bit difference plus the standardised descriptor difference, and fit a LightGBM regressor with L1 loss on the target y_i minus y_j. At prediction time, for each test molecule, take its predicted difference against 100 random training anchors, add each anchor's true y, and average the results. Return the median of these estimates as the base prediction. Use the seed to choose the pairs, and keep the output a single column so it can join the stack.

title: Trimmed training: drop the largest out-of-fold residuals before the final fit
spec: Within fit_predict, after the inner 5-fold OOF stacking produces oof predictions, compute the absolute residual |oof_meta - y| for each training row. Remove the 5% of training rows with the largest residuals (and their descriptor, fingerprint and group entries) from the training matrices. Refit the full base_predict and meta Ridge on the trimmed set and predict the test set. The goal is to stop mislabelled or assay-noisy molecules from dominating the L2-type kernel fit and the tree splits. Keep the evaluation on the untrimmed test fold unchanged.

title: Scaffold-aware sample weighting
spec: Compute the Bemis-Murcko scaffold of each training molecule and weight each sample by the inverse square root of how many training molecules share its scaffold. This stops over-represented scaffold families from dominating the fit, which matters because the test folds hold out whole scaffolds. Pass the weights as sample_weight to the random forest fit.

title: Rank-Gaussian target transform with quantile back-mapping
spec: Before base_predict is called, map the training targets y to normal scores: rank each y_i within the training fold, convert ranks to quantiles (r-0.5)/n, and apply scipy.stats.norm.ppf. Train all base learners and the meta Ridge on these transformed targets. For the final predictions, map each predicted normal score back to the target scale by taking the training-target quantile at the same Gaussian probability (np.quantile of the training y at norm.cdf(score)), clipped to the observed range. This reshapes the skewed logD distribution so the L2-based kernel ridge fit spends less effort on the tails.

title: Extra-trees mode and per-node feature sampling in LightGBM
spec: In lgb_params, add extra_trees=True (random thresholds per split) and feature_fraction_bynode=0.5 on top of the existing feature_fraction. Keep the (31, 10, 0.2) config and 600 rounds, and raise num_boost_round to 900 because randomised splits converge more slowly. This is a single-line regularisation change to the LightGBM base learner with no added search or extra fits, so the cost per fit is almost unchanged.

title: Gobbi 2D pharmacophore Tanimoto kernel member
spec: Add a kernel ridge stack member whose kernel is Tanimoto similarity on Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprints (rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Gobbi_Pharm2D with the default factory, converted to a bit vector of fixed length, for example 1024 bits via fold or by taking the first 1024 positions). Compute the fingerprint for each molecule inside fit_predict, pass it to base_predict, and build the kernel with the existing tanimoto() helper. Fix lam=0.5 and wr=1.0 and skip any inner search. Append the member's out-of-fold prediction as an additional column to the stacking matrix so the Ridge meta-learner can weight it. This is a bold, cheap member that captures topological pharmacophore pairs rather than bit paths.

title: Ergonomic reduced-graph (ErG) kernel member
spec: Add a fourth stack member: a kernel ridge model whose kernel is the Tanimoto similarity on ErG reduced-graph fingerprints (rdkit.Chem.rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint, stored as a float vector per molecule). Compute the fingerprints in fit_predict alongside the Morgan ones, pass them into base_predict, and normalise each one to unit L2 norm before the Tanimoto computation so that the same tanimoto() helper applies. Use the same lam and wr grid as the existing kernel member, with a single fixed choice (lam=0.5, wr=1.0) to keep the cost low. Append its column to the output of base_predict so the Ridge meta-learner receives four columns. This adds a pharmacophore-level similarity view that the bit-level Morgan kernel cannot express.

title: Monotone LightGBM constraint on Crippen MolLogP
spec: In base_predict's LightGBM member, add a monotone_constraints entry so the model's predictions are non-decreasing in the RDKit MolLogP descriptor. Find the column index as 2*N_BITS plus the position of 'MolLogP' in [n for n, _ in Descriptors._descList]. Build a list of zeros of length Xa.shape[1] with +1 at that index and pass it as monotone_constraints=... in lgb_params (and keep monotone_constraints_method default). Everything else, including the 600 rounds and the (31, 10, 0.2) config, stays the same. This encodes the physical prior that higher lipophilicity means higher logD, which the trees currently have to learn from data.

title: Gradient-boosted meta-learner with descriptors
spec: Replace the positive Ridge meta-learner with a shallow LightGBM regressor trained with objective regression_l1 on the three OOF base predictions plus four physchem columns (MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors). Use num_leaves 7, min_child_samples 40, learning_rate 0.03, and 300 rounds. Keep the feature order fixed so the test columns line up. The purpose is to let the meta-learner correct base-learner bias as a function of size and polarity. Fall back to the Ridge result if the meta predictions are not finite.

title: Random-forest leaf-proximity kernel as a stack member
spec: Add a fourth base learner to base_predict: the random-forest proximity kernel. Fit the existing RandomForestRegressor (min_samples_leaf=5, max_features=0.3, 200 trees) on the training part. Get leaf indices with rf.apply(X) for the training and prediction rows. Build a one-hot leaf matrix per tree, sum over trees, and divide by the number of trees to get the proximity kernel P (training by training, and prediction by training). Predict with kernel ridge using a fixed lam=0.5 and no grid search: alpha = solve(P_tr + 0.5*I, y - mu), prediction = P_te @ alpha + mu. Append this column to the base predictions. The meta-learner then weights it against the other members.

title: Laplacian kernel on ECFP count vectors as a separate member
spec: Add a fourth kernel member to base_predict: a Laplacian kernel on the count ECFP vector. Compute D = L1 distance between count-based ECFP vectors (use Morgan count fingerprints from GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy, radius 2, 1024 bits), then K = exp(-D / s) with s set to the median training L1 distance. Fit kernel ridge with lam=0.5 and no grid search, and append the prediction as one more base-learner column. The meta-learner decides how much weight it gets. This is a different inductive bias from the Tanimoto and RBF kernels already in the stack.

title: Random-subspace bagged kernel ridge member
spec: Make the kernel-ridge member an ensemble of 8 kernel ridge fits, each on a random 50% subset of the ECFP bit columns (drawn with np.random.default_rng(seed + j)). Each subset gives its own Tanimoto kernel, computed on the selected columns, while the RBF descriptor kernel stays as it is. Average the 8 predictions for each row and use that average as the kernel member's output in the stack. The lam and wr values stay at the current inner-CV selection (computed once on the full bit set) so the extra cost is only the 8 solves with the fixed hyperparameters. This decorrelates the kernel member from the forest and the boosted model through feature bagging.
